clusters.label: Automated Observation in Complex Systems
clusters.description: This cluster investigates the deployment of automated sensing and decision-making technologies in complex, high-stakes environments, ranging from safety-critical logistics to marine wildlife monitoring. It focuses on the capabilities, limitations, and observational insights provided by machine-based systems compared to traditional human or manual methods.
clusters.rationale: The two papers are thematically distinct: one is a philosophical/technical inquiry into AI trust in logistics, while the other is a biological study using camera technology for shark behavior. The only strong commonality is the use of automated/technological systems to observe or manage complex, high-risk environments. The label is broad to accommodate this significant divergence, resulting in lower confidence.

clusters.label: Human-Centered AI Interaction Design
clusters.description: This cluster focuses on the design principles, user agency, and ethical considerations of integrating AI into human-facing systems, specifically addressing how to maintain user autonomy, reduce cognitive load, and ensure responsible deployment in administrative, immersive, and educational contexts.
clusters.rationale: All three papers share a core concern with the human-AI interface and the preservation of user agency. Paper 1 applies UCD to administrative AI support, Paper 2 critiques AI attention guidance in immersive environments to protect user autonomy, and Paper 3 reviews generative AI in education with a focus on responsible, mediated use rather than substitution. The unifying theme is the design and governance of AI systems to serve human needs without eroding user control or judgment.

clusters.label: AI-Driven Enterprise Strategic Agility
clusters.description: This cluster investigates how artificial intelligence and real-time business intelligence frameworks enhance enterprise strategic agility, decision-making speed, and the formation of new-quality productive forces through data-driven organizational transformation.
clusters.rationale: Both papers focus on the intersection of AI/data analytics and enterprise strategy. Paper 1 empirically links real-time BI to strategic agility, while Paper 2 theorizes how AI and the digital economy drive productive force transformation. The common thread is the use of intelligent data systems to improve organizational responsiveness and strategic outcomes.

clusters.label: Quantitative Socio-Economic Impact Assessment
clusters.description: This cluster focuses on the statistical evaluation of economic, social, and policy-related impacts within specific industries or public health sectors. It involves using quantitative methods to assess resource value, financial burden, or market dynamics to inform strategic development or policy interventions.
clusters.rationale: Both papers employ quantitative statistical methods (regression, factor analysis) to assess socio-economic factors (cultural resource value, catastrophic health expenditure) within specific domains (cultural heritage, public health). While the domain is 'AI decision making', these papers represent the data analysis and impact assessment components often used to inform decision-making strategies in industrial or public sectors, rather than the AI algorithms themselves. The shared thread is the quantitative evaluation of economic/social variables to guide strategy.

clusters.label: Algorithmic Governance and Regulatory Compliance
clusters.description: This cluster focuses on the legal, policy, and empirical evaluation of regulatory frameworks governing algorithmic systems, specifically examining how jurisdictions like China, South Korea, and the EU structure oversight of AI journalism, platform competition, and model transparency.
clusters.rationale: All three papers address the intersection of law/policy and algorithmic systems. Paper 1 analyzes communication policies for AI journalism in East Asia, Paper 2 reconstructs antitrust theories for algorithmic platform governance in China, and Paper 3 empirically assesses the impact of the EU AI Act on model transparency. The unifying theme is the structural and empirical analysis of how regulatory regimes govern algorithmic decision-making and deployment.

clusters.label: AI-Driven Industrial Safety and Maintenance
clusters.description: This cluster focuses on the application of artificial intelligence and digital twin technologies to enhance operational safety, predictive maintenance, and fault-tolerant control in industrial and logistics environments, emphasizing human-in-the-loop governance and risk mitigation.
clusters.rationale: The cluster unites papers on AI applications in industrial settings, specifically focusing on safety, maintenance, and system reliability. Paper 1 addresses AI safety and governance in logistics, Paper 2 details digital-twin-driven predictive maintenance for agricultural machinery, and Paper 3 provides the underlying sensor hardware for physiological/industrial monitoring. The common thread is the use of AI/automation to improve safety and operational reliability in physical industrial systems.

clusters.label: Interpretable Anomaly Detection in Industry
clusters.description: This cluster focuses on developing machine learning models for industrial and clinical decision-making that prioritize transparency, interpretability, and reliability. It addresses the challenge of deploying AI in high-stakes environments by combining statistical grounding, calibration, or advanced kernel methods to ensure predictions are auditable and robust against overlapping data distributions.
clusters.rationale: Both papers address the deployment of AI in critical sectors (medicine and industry) where black-box models are insufficient. Paper 1 emphasizes interpretability and calibration for clinical classification, while Paper 2 focuses on improving anomaly detection performance in industrial settings using quantum kernels. The shared theme is the enhancement of AI decision-making reliability and transparency in specialized, high-stakes domains.
